sum: Eight days from Syabrubesi through Gatlang and over the 3,842 m Pangsang La to Tipling, Shertung and Chalish below Ganesh Himal, sleeping in family homes, then out by jeep to Dhading Besi.

guide.note: You enter through Langtang National Park, where the permit is checked at Dhunche, and the Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers to hire a licensed guide since April 2023, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. The Dhading villages lie outside any park. Take a guide in any case: homestays have no signboards and need a phone call ahead, few people on the route speak English, and since the 2026 flood only someone in touch with the villages knows which roads and bridges are open.

access: The classic start is Syabrubesi, seven to nine hours from Kathmandu by bus. The finish is Dhading Besi, three to five hours from Kathmandu, reached by a long jeep ride from the roadhead below Borang. Both were hit by the flood of 26 August 2026: the road was cut short of Syabrubesi, with vehicles stopping at Dhunche, and the Trishuli bridge near Malekhu that links Dhading Besi to the Prithvi Highway was swept away, leaving a detour on back roads. We found no report by November 2026 that either had been fully restored. Ask your agency what is open at both ends in the week you travel.

photo.a: The sun sets over a sea of cloud below the dark, reddish slopes of the Pangsang La, with a line of snow peaks on the horizon to the right.
photo.c: Sunset over a sea of cloud from the Pangsang La, 3,842 m

permits.name: Langtang National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park checkpoint in Dhunche on the drive to Syabrubesi, or in advance at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Bus or a jeep seat from Kathmandu to Syabrubesi
transportExtra: the jeep from Borang to Dhading Besi and the bus on to Kathmandu
tips: Carry all your cash from Kathmandu, in small notes. There is no cash machine on the trek until Dhading Besi.
Bring a sleeping bag. Homestay bedding is thin, and Somdang is cold at 3,271 m.
You eat with the family, at their hours and from their pot. Agree the price for bed and meals when you arrive.
Carry lunch and at least two litres of water on both pass days. Tea shops are few and may be shut.
Dress modestly in the villages, and ask before photographing people, shrines or a shaman at work.

days.note: The same long road day as for Langtang, through Trishuli Bazaar and Dhunche, where the park permit is checked. Since the August 2026 flood vehicles have been stopping short of Syabrubesi, so you may finish on foot or sleep in Dhunche. Fix the plan with your agency before you leave Kathmandu.

A steep two-hour climb west to the Rongga Bhanjyang saddle, then a gentler traverse above the terraces of Goljung to Gatlang, partly on a dirt road. The lodges and homestays here are the most comfortable beds of the trek. If you arrive early, walk through the old houses to the gompa.

days.t: Gatlang to Somdang over the Khurpu Bhanjyang
days.note: An hour up to Parvati Kunda, then a long climb through pine and rhododendron forest to the herders' huts at Yuri Kharka, the usual lunch stop, and on to the pass at about 3,720 m. An hour or more downhill brings you to the simple lodges at Somdang. You sleep 1,000 m higher than last night, so expect a mild headache.
why: A climb of 1,033 m in one day, to sleep at 3,271 m. Go slowly, drink plenty, and say so if you get a headache.

days.t: Somdang to Tipling over the Pangsang La
days.note: Two to three hours up, on trail and stretches of rough road, to the open saddle of the Pangsang La, where a simple lodge stands and the view takes in Ganesh Himal and Manaslu. Then the knees take over: about 1,750 m of descent through forest and pasture to the terraces of Tipling. Start early and carry lunch.

days.t: Tipling to Chalish by way of Shertung
days.note: A short day. Drop to the bridge over the Adha Khola, climb to Shertung, a large Tamang village on the facing hillside, and walk on down to Chalish, where Gurung, Ghale and Kami families run the homestays. Give the afternoon to the village, and ask your host whether a dance evening can be arranged.

An easy walk through forest and terraced fields to Borang, which some itineraries time at two hours and others at five. With time in hand, spend the morning in Chalish and set out after lunch. Have your host or guide book jeep seats for tomorrow as soon as you arrive.

days.t: Borang to Dhading Besi by jeep
days.note: Walk down to wherever the jeeps are starting that season, often by the Lishne Khola below the village, then ride five to seven hours on a rough hill road to the district town. It is a slow, dusty journey and the worst road of the trip. Dhading Besi has ordinary hotels, hot water and cash machines.

days.t: Drive from Dhading Besi to Kathmandu
days.note: In normal times a sealed road runs down to Malekhu on the Prithvi Highway and east to Kathmandu. The bridge over the Trishuli there was lost in the August 2026 flood and traffic has been using a longer detour, so ask about the route in Dhading Besi and allow most of the day.
